timeline.title: The Bene Israel arrival narrative
timeline.body: Bene Israel tradition holds that the community's ancestors reached the Konkan coast of western India roughly 2,500 years ago after a shipwreck. This is a community account of origin. It is transmitted within the community rather than established by documentary evidence, and historians differ on dating.

timeline.title: Copper plate grants to the Jews of Kerala
timeline.body: Rulers in the Malabar region issued copper plates to the Jewish community, recording the grant of privileges and standing. The plates are among the most cited pieces of material evidence for organised Jewish settlement in southern India.

timeline.title: Relocation from Kodungallur to Kochi
timeline.body: The Jewish community relocated from Kodungallur, establishing the settlement in Kochi that came to be known as Jew Town.

timeline.title: The Paradesi Synagogue is built in Kochi
timeline.body: Built in Kochi, Kerala, by the city's Jewish trading community, including Sephardic families who had been exiled from Spain and Portugal. It is India's oldest synagogue, and in the early twenty-first century was the Cochin community's only active synagogue.

timeline.title: The Sassoon family arrives in Bombay
timeline.body: The Sassoon family arrived in Bombay in 1832, part of the nineteenth century movement of Baghdadi Jews leaving Iraq and other lands. David Sassoon went on to build institutions in the city that still serve Indian society.

timeline.title: India recognises the State of Israel
timeline.body: India formally recognised Israel on 17 September 1950. Full diplomatic relations, however, would not follow for another forty-two years. The gap between these two dates is one of the central questions in the history of the relationship.

timeline.title: Full diplomatic relations established
timeline.body: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, opening embassies and beginning the modern phase of the relationship. Nearly every strand of cooperation that exists today, in agriculture, water, defence, science and trade, was built after this point.

timeline.title: Agreement on cooperation in science and technology
timeline.body: One of the first framework agreements after 1992, establishing the basis for joint scientific work.

timeline.title: Agreement on agricultural cooperation
timeline.body: The agricultural cooperation agreement signed in 1993 became the spine of what is now the most visible civilian strand of the relationship. It was renewed in April 2025.

timeline.title: Memorandum on the industrial research and development initiative
timeline.body: Signed in May 2005, extending cooperation from academic science into industrial research and development.

timeline.title: President Pranab Mukherjee visits Israel
timeline.body: A visit at the level of head of state, preceding the shift in tempo that followed in 2017 and 2018.

timeline.title: President Reuven Rivlin visits India
timeline.body: The return visit at head of state level. A memorandum on water resources management was signed in the same month.

timeline.title: Memorandum on water resources management
timeline.body: Water is the strand where the two countries' problems most closely resemble each other: scarcity, salinity, and the need to grow more with less.

timeline.title: Prime Minister Modi visits Israel
timeline.body: A visit from 4 to 6 July 2017. In Tel Aviv the Prime Minister addressed a gathering of approximately 8,000 people of Indian origin and Indian nationals. A set of memoranda was signed during the visit.

timeline.title: India-Israel Industrial Research and Development and Technological Innovation Fund
timeline.body: Known as I4F. Established in 2017 and renewed for the period 2023 to 2027.

timeline.title: Prime Minister Netanyahu visits India
timeline.body: A six day visit to India from 14 to 19 January 2018, the reciprocal leg of the exchange begun the previous July.

timeline.title: INS Tarangini port call in Israel
timeline.body: A naval port call by the Indian sail training ship, following earlier Indian naval port calls in May 2017.

timeline.title: Agreement on cooperation in the field of health
timeline.body: Signed on 21 December 2020.

timeline.title: Israel ratifies the International Solar Alliance framework
timeline.body: Israel's ratification brought it into the India-initiated International Solar Alliance.

timeline.title: Indian Air Force participates in Exercise Blue Flag
timeline.body: Indian Air Force participation in the multinational exercise hosted by Israel.

timeline.title: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar visits Israel
timeline.body: A visit from 17 to 21 October 2021.

timeline.title: Adani-led consortium acquires Haifa Port
timeline.body: The acquisition, valued at USD 1.18 billion, is the single largest Indian commercial commitment in Israel to date and connects the relationship to the wider question of Indian Ocean to Mediterranean logistics.

timeline.title: First talks at Defence Minister level
timeline.body: The first engagement at the level of Defence Minister, on 3 March 2023.

timeline.title: India-Israel Innovation Centre for Agriculture declared
timeline.body: Declared in May 2023, alongside a letter of intent on water technology centres of excellence.

timeline.title: Operation Ajay
timeline.body: Between 12 and 22 October 2023, over 1,300 people were evacuated from Israel under Operation Ajay.

timeline.title: Prime Minister Modi meets President Herzog at COP 28
timeline.body: A meeting on the margins of COP 28 on 1 December 2023.

timeline.title: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval visits Israel
timeline.body: A visit on 11 and 12 March 2024.

timeline.title: Agricultural cooperation agreement renewed
timeline.body: The 1993 agreement was renewed in April 2025, extending the framework under which the centres of excellence operate.

timeline.title: Joint postage stamp on Holi and Purim
timeline.body: A joint stamp issue pairing Holi and Purim, released during the visit of the Israeli Economy Minister from 11 to 13 February 2025. Two festivals of colour, noise and reversal, issued on one sheet.

timeline.title: Cyber Policy Dialogue
timeline.body: Held on 27 March 2025.

timeline.title: Operation Sindhu
timeline.body: Around 818 people were evacuated between 22 and 25 June 2025 under Operation Sindhu.

timeline.title: Bilateral Investment Agreement signed
timeline.body: Signed during the visit of the Israeli Finance Minister from 8 to 10 September 2025. Investment protection is the legal groundwork that has to exist before capital moves at scale.

timeline.title: Export Control Dialogue
timeline.body: Held on 27 and 28 October 2025.

timeline.title: Memorandum of understanding on defence cooperation
timeline.body: Signed on 4 November 2025, alongside the seventeenth meeting of the Joint Working Group on defence.

timeline.title: Terms of reference agreed for a free trade agreement
timeline.body: Agreed during the visit of the Indian Commerce and Industry Minister from 20 to 22 November 2025. Terms of reference are the starting gun for negotiation, not the agreement itself.

timeline.title: Sushma Swaraj Institute and Israeli Foreign Ministry memorandum
timeline.body: A memorandum between India's diplomatic training institute and the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, signed in November 2025.

timeline.title: Joint Work Plan 2026 agreed
timeline.body: Agreed during the External Affairs Minister's visit to Israel on 16 and 17 December 2025.

timeline.title: India Chair established at Tel Aviv University
timeline.body: An agreement between the Indian Council for Cultural Relations and Tel Aviv University for an India Chair, in December 2025.

timeline.title: Joint declaration on fisheries and aquaculture
timeline.body: Signed during the visit of India's Minister of Fisheries from 13 to 15 January 2026.

timeline.title: India votes against Israel's admission to the United Nations
timeline.body: Resolution 273 (III), on the admission of Israel to membership of the United Nations, was adopted at the 207th plenary meeting on 11 May 1949. India voted against, and has been described as the only non-Arab state to do so. Sixteen months later India recognised Israel. Both facts belong in any honest account of the origin of this relationship.

timeline.title: India recognises the Palestine Liberation Organisation
timeline.body: India is recorded as the first non-Arab state to recognise the Palestine Liberation Organisation.

timeline.title: India recognises the State of Palestine
timeline.body: Four years before establishing full diplomatic relations with Israel.

timeline.title: India votes to revoke the resolution equating Zionism with racism
timeline.body: Described as the first occasion on which India formally and openly voted in favour of Israel at the General Assembly. Full diplomatic relations followed within about a month.

timeline.title: The comprehensive agricultural work plan begins
timeline.body: The 1993 agreement acquired an operating structure. The Indo-Israel Agricultural Project has since run in phases: 2009 to 2012, 2012 to 2015, 2015 to 2018, 2018 to 2020, 2021 to 2023, and a sixth work plan covering 2024 to 2026.

timeline.title: The Union Cabinet approves the water resources memorandum
timeline.body: Covering efficient water use, micro irrigation, recycling and reuse of waste water, desalination, aquifer recharge and in situ conservation, with a joint working group to monitor it.

timeline.title: Seven agreements signed during the visit, two of them on water
timeline.body: One memorandum on water conservation between India's Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation and Israel's Ministry of National Infrastructure, Energy and Water Resources. A second on state water utility reforms, between that Israeli ministry and Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam. A three year work programme in agriculture was also signed.

timeline.title: India's first private missile subsystems plant opens in Hyderabad
timeline.body: Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems, a joint venture with the Kalyani Group at 51 per cent and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems at 49 per cent. The pattern to notice is that the cooperation moved from purchase to manufacture inside India.

timeline.title: The Indian Air Force takes part in Blue Flag for the first time
timeline.body: Alongside the United States, Italy, France, Germany, Greece and Poland. In the 2021 edition, held from 17 to 28 October, five upgraded Indian Mirage 2000 fighters took part.

timeline.title: The first four projects are awarded under the innovation fund
timeline.body: The India-Israel Industrial Research and Development and Technological Innovation Fund is a forty million dollar fund, twenty million from each side, funded by India's Department of Science and Technology and the Israel Innovation Authority.

timeline.title: A drone plant opens in Hyderabad
timeline.body: Adani Defence and Aerospace with Elbit Systems, described as the first unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturing facility in India and the first outside Israel to make the Hermes 900.

timeline.title: The first MRSAM firing unit is handed to the Indian Air Force
timeline.body: At Air Force Station Jaisalmer. The Defence Research and Development Organisation states that it developed the Medium Range Surface to Air Missile system jointly with Israel Aerospace Industries, that it is capable of engaging multiple targets at ranges up to 70 kilometres, and that a number of firing units have been delivered to the Air Force and the Army.

timeline.title: The fifth Indo-Israel agriculture work programme is signed
timeline.body: Between India's Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Israel's MASHAV. At the time twenty-nine Centres of Excellence were operational across twelve states, producing more than 25 million vegetable seedlings and more than 387 thousand fruit plants. The Villages of Excellence initiative was launched alongside it.

timeline.title: Three Centres of Excellence open in Karnataka
timeline.body: At Kolar for mango, Bagalkote for pomegranate and Dharwad for vegetables, with a combined capacity of 50,000 grafts and 25 lakh vegetable seedlings a year.

timeline.title: The India-Israel Center of Water Technology is agreed at IIT Madras
timeline.body: A letter of intent signed in New Delhi covering integrated water resources management, urban water supply, water recycling, monitoring, harvesting and data management, in support of India's AMRUT mission. A parallel centre was agreed at IIT Roorkee.

timeline.title: The framework agreement on Indian workers in Israel
timeline.body: The Agreement on Facilitation of the Temporary Employment of Indian Workers in Specific Labour Market Sectors in the State of Israel, with an implementation protocol for construction workers. Accounts differ on when it was concluded: the Indian government states in Parliament that it was signed in November 2023, while other accounts date the understanding to the Israeli foreign minister's visit to India in May 2023.

timeline.title: The first batch of Indian construction workers flies to Israel
timeline.body: More than sixty workers, after recruitment centres were set up in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana in January 2024. By 22 July 2024 the figure given in the Lok Sabha was 4,825 workers, the largest number from Uttar Pradesh, with a stated entitlement to equal treatment on labour rights with Israeli citizens.

timeline.title: India abstains on the emergency session resolution on Gaza
timeline.body: Resolution A/RES/ES-10/21 was adopted at the 41st plenary meeting of the tenth emergency special session. India abstained, citing the absence of all elements of its approach in the text. Vote counts reported for this resolution differ between sources.

timeline.title: India votes for the ceasefire resolution
timeline.body: The General Assembly demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and humanitarian access. The vote was 153 in favour, 10 against, 23 abstentions. India voted in favour.

timeline.title: India votes for Palestinian full membership of the United Nations
timeline.body: The vote was 143 in favour, 9 against, 25 abstentions.

timeline.title: India abstains on the resolution following the ICJ advisory opinion
timeline.body: The resolution demanded that Israel end its presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territory within twelve months. The vote was 124 in favour, 14 against, 43 abstentions. India abstained, alongside Australia, Canada, Germany, Italy, Nepal, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.

timeline.title: India votes for the New York Declaration on a two state solution
timeline.body: The vote was 142 in favour, 10 against, 12 abstentions.

timeline.title: Agriculture agreements signed in New Delhi
timeline.body: Between Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Israeli Agriculture Minister Avi Dichter, with emphasis on climate resilient seed development.

timeline.title: Terms of reference for the free trade agreement are signed in Tel Aviv
timeline.body: By Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Israeli Economy and Industry Minister Nir Barkat.

timeline.title: Prime Minister Modi's state visit to Israel and address to the Knesset
timeline.body: Sixteen memoranda were signed and the relationship was elevated to a Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity. It was the first address to the Knesset by an Indian Prime Minister. The joint statement records that 35 Centres of Excellence were operating with eight more being jointly operationalised, that more than a million Indian farmers had been trained at them, and that up to 50,000 additional Indian workers may arrive in Israel within five years.

timeline.title: The first round of free trade agreement negotiations
timeline.body: Held in New Delhi, covering trade in goods and services, rules of origin, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade, customs procedures, intellectual property and digital trade. A second round was scheduled for May 2026 in Israel.

timeline.title: The Bilateral Investment Agreement enters into force
timeline.body: Signed on 8 September 2025 in New Delhi by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, it provides protection against expropriation, transparency, transfer rights, compensation for losses and an independent arbitration mechanism. Total bilateral investment stood at USD 800 million when it was signed.
